journey.title: Open the filters drawer, land on its autofocus search field, and apply a filter with the keyboard
journey.goal: Opening the drawer moves focus into it, so the user can tick a filter and show results without a pointer

functionalJourney.title: Apply a filter with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking Filters, ticking Waterproof and clicking Show results applies the filter

guards.title: Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to Filters
guards.goal: After opening the drawer with the pointer, Escape closes it and focus is back on the Filters button

plan.root_cause: The dialog's autofocus attribute is not honored when opening via showModal(), causing focus to remain outside the dialog after it opens.
plan.repair_strategy: After showing the dialog (showModal/show), explicitly focus the element with the autofocus attribute, falling back to the dialog itself if none found.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus moves into the drawer when opened, allowing users to interact with filters without a pointer.
functional_risks: Potential focus theft if autofocus element is not focusable.
Risk of double-focus if browser already moved focus (mitigated by checking existence).
verification_requirements: After activating the drawer button with Enter, focus is on #filters-search.
Pressing Tab moves focus to #in-stock checkbox.
Closing the drawer with Escape returns focus to the trigger button.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus moves into the drawer when opened, landing on the search field so users can immediately type or Tab to filters without a pointer.

plan.root_cause: The native dialog.showModal() does not reliably focus the autofocus element in this environment. Previous synchronous focus attempts in _showElement race with browser focus management, leaving focus on the trigger or body.
plan.repair_strategy: In DialogBase._show, after calling _showElement, yield to the microtask queue (await Promise.resolve()) then explicitly focus the autofocus element (or dialog fallback). This allows native focus management to complete before we set focus.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus moves into the drawer when opened, landing on the search field so users can immediately type or Tab to filters without a pointer.
functional_risks: Potential focus theft if autofocus element is not focusable (mitigated by fallback to dialog).
Risk of double-focus if browser already moved focus (mitigated by yielding to microtask).
verification_requirements: After activating the drawer button with Enter, focus is on #filters-search.
Pressing Tab moves focus to #in-stock checkbox.
Closing the drawer with Escape returns focus to the trigger button.

plan.root_cause: The native <dialog> element's showModal() does not reliably focus the autofocus element in this environment. The Drawer component (which extends DialogBase) lacks explicit focus management after opening, leaving keyboard focus on the trigger button or body instead of moving into the drawer.
plan.repair_strategy: Override _show in Drawer to await the base show lifecycle (which handles animations and fires 'shown'), then explicitly focus the autofocus element (or fall back to the dialog itself) so keyboard users land inside the drawer immediately.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus moves into the drawer when opened, landing on the search field so users can immediately type or Tab to filters without a pointer.
functional_risks: Potential focus theft if autofocus element is not focusable (mitigated by fallback to dialog).
Risk of double-focus if browser already moved focus (mitigated by awaiting base show completion).
verification_requirements: After activating the drawer button with Enter, focus is on #filters-search.
Pressing Tab moves focus to #in-stock checkbox.
Closing the drawer with Escape returns focus to the trigger button.
